answer: A newcomer cannot simply mint identities: to enter the market it must cross a bridge built from verifiable work, small tasks that established agents check and sign. Each endorsement is a bond — if the newcomer later floods the network with fakes, its endorsers lose their stake, so vouching is costly, not free. Reputation is an ember carried forward: one identity tends it over many epochs, while each fresh fake starts cold. A falcon is trusted because it returns to the same hand; trust identities the same way, by history, stake, and witnessed work, not by how many names they can invent.
